title: Constants & iota
focus: const declarations, iota enum pattern, typed vs untyped constants
rules: Define Weekday type and iota-based constants
IsWeekend and NextDay use the enum correctly

flashcards.back: A special identifier that auto-increments in const declarations. Starts at 0 and increments by 1 for each const spec.

flashcards.front: How do you create an enum in Go?
flashcards.back: Use const with iota: const ( A = iota; B; C ) gives A=0, B=1, C=2.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between typed and untyped constants?
flashcards.back: Typed constants (const x int = 1) have a fixed type. Untyped constants (const x = 1) can be used with any compatible type.

flashcards.front: Can you take the address of a constant?
flashcards.back: No. Constants are computed at compile time and have no address in memory.
